key_insight: An on-the-fly Δ-machine learned force field combines a Yukawa reference model with learned DFT corrections to simulate warm dense matter accurately at up to 1,000× the speed of ab initio molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient prediction of equation-of-state, structural, and transport properties of warm dense magnesium under extreme conditions.
method: Fit a Yukawa model on the fly to capture dominant screened-Coulomb ion interactions.
Use kernel learning and Bayesian linear regression to learn energy, force, and stress corrections relative to Kohn–Sham DFT.
Apply the corrected force field in molecular dynamics simulations.
evidence_signal: Validation against published warm dense carbon DFT results showed lower errors than standard MLFF at comparable cost; magnesium simulations covered 5.22–10.44 g/cm³ and 600 kK–1.5 MK.
watch_item: Accuracy outside the studied materials and conditions remains to be established, and on-the-fly fitting still requires DFT reference calculations.
paper_title: On-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
